examiner: What is Free sparring?
question: Free Sparring
answer:
Jayoo Matsoki: The aim in free sparring is to score points. You are using Taekwon-Do as a sport.
The scoring system awards 1 point for a hand technique to middle or high section, 2 points for a middle kick, and 3 points for a high kick.
The objective is only to touch your partner without causing any pain or injury.
No techniques are allowed below the belt.

examiner: Describe Connection Motion
question: Connecting Motion
answer: is used when a no-tension-on-impact technique is connected to a tension-on-impact technique. Hooking blocks are no-tension-on-impact — these are executed by inhaling through the whole of the block and then exhaling before moving on. In pattern Yul-Gok, a hooking block is connected to an obverse punch — this is executed by inhaling on the block and exhaling on the punch.

examiner: What is the meaning of Choong-Moo?
question: Choong-Moo meaning
answer: Choong-Moo was the given name of the great Admiral Yi Sun-Sin of the Yi Dynasty. He was reputed to have invented the first armoured battleship, the Kobukson, which was the precursor of the present-day submarine in 1592 A.D. The pattern ends with a left-hand attack to symbolise his regrettable death, having no chance to show his unrestrained potential, checked by his loyalty to the king

examiner: What is Step Turn in korean, and describe it?
question:
STEP TURN
(korean & description)
answer:
OMGYO DIDIMYO DOLGI
Allows any change in direction from 01 to 360 degrees. Can be executed with either foot moving forward, backward, clockwise, anti-clockwise and can be combined with double stepping, shifting and / or sliding.

examiner: What is Spot Turn in korean, and describe it?
question:
SPOT TURN
(korean & description)
answer:
GUJARI DOLGI
Only turn 180 degrees to face an opponent behind, with this method both feet move to complete the turn. Generally the front foot will move first but on occasion the back foot can be moved first. The turn is executed after moving one foot onto the centreline of the stance and can be taken clockwise or anti-clockwise depending which leg is forward. On completion the front leg will be the opposite one to before the turn.

examiner: What is the THEORY OF POWER & brief explanation?
question: THEORY OF POWER & brief explanation.
answer:
REACTION FORCE. Use their force, strike when your opponent moves in.
CONCENTRATION. Direct power to a small point, & tension to a split second.
EQUILIBRIUM. Use reaction arm for dynamic stability. Keep body in balance.
BREATH CONTROL. Tense abdomen to breathe out on impact.
MASS. Use hip twist and knee spring to increase body weight.
SPEED. The most essential factor for power, however all the other factors contribute to speed.
